sec: Bone constituents and the collagen-type table · p864

items.q: Cells contribute what percentage of bone, with matrix making the rest?
Match matrix fraction — 1) Organic  2) Inorganic … A) Calcium, phosphorous, magnesium (60–70%)  B) Type I collagen + non-collagenous proteins (30–40%)
items.exp: Organic 30–40% (type I collagen predominant); inorganic 60–70% (Ca, P, Mg). (Book p864)

items.q: The predominant organic constituent of bone matrix is:
items.exp: Type I collagen is predominant among organic constituents. (Book p864)

items.q: Matrix GLA protein functions as an inhibitor of vascular calcification; it is inhibited by:
items.exp: Matrix GLA protein inhibits vascular calcification; warfarin (vit K antagonist) inhibits it → precipitates calcification. (Book p864)

items.q: The non-collagenous proteins listed are osteopontin, osteocalcin, thrombospondin, matrix GLA protein, fibronectin and:
items.exp: The sixth listed non-collagenous protein is proteoglycans. (Book p864)

items.q: Match collagen type to disorder — 1) Type I  2) Type III  3) Type IV  4) Type VII … A) EDS type IV (vascular)  B) Epidermolysis bullosa  C) Osteogenesis imperfecta  D) Alport/Goodpasture
items.exp: Type I → OI (also EDS VII/arthrochalasia, osteoporosis); type III → EDS IV vascular; type IV → Alport/Goodpasture; type VII → epidermolysis bullosa. (Book p864)

items.q: Type II collagen is distributed in cartilage and vitreous humor; its disorder association is:
items.exp: Type II (cartilage, vitreous humor) → chondrodysplasia. (Book p864)

items.q: Which collagen type is NOT linked to a named disorder in the table?
items.exp: Type 8 (endothelium) has no listed disorder (−). (Book p864)
